messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: multiple OOMs detected on pool 'inference-gtx12' (nodes 12-17). Incident ID INC-2026-042. Autoscaler suppressed due to oom_surge. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-042

sarah.lee: seeing steady memory growth on the KV shards, looks like slow leak rather than a single big allocation. paging rate for attention pages spiked ~45m ago.

devon: confirmed. node-14 has repeated CUDA errors in logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:04Z] runtime: WARNING: attention_pager.cpp: page_in failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-15T03:12:04Z] runtime: ERROR: container exited with code 137 (OOM)
[2026-03-15T03:12:05Z] kubelet: CrashLoopBackOff (restart 3x)
```

mina: adding graphs: kv-cache-resident-bytes shows monotonic climb over last 6 hours on shard-7 (no big GC). eviction_rate is near zero despite high pressure.

ravi: is compaction job running? last compaction for that shard was 36h ago. we should trigger an immediate compact + aggressive eviction.

oncall-sre: can we run the admin cache-sweep endpoint? last time running cache-sweep dropped resident by ~20% temporarily.

mina: yes, admin API available. endpoint: `POST /admin/kv/shards/7/sweep?force=true` - will mark cold prefixes for eviction and kick compaction. note: it will increase latency for affected requests while hot sharding migrates.

devon: rolling mitigation plan: 1) run sweep on shard-7; 2) temporarily lower KV cache threshold to 0.6 for pool 'inference-gtx12'; 3) enable model-fallback to cpu-compact variant for long contexts; 4) cordon node-14 and drain if it keeps OOMing.

ops-bot: ACTION_CREATED: /admin/kv/shards/7/sweep triggered by @devon at 2966660048. Job: sweep-2966660048.

ravi: running the curl now from jump-host:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  "https://control-plane.internal/admin/kv/shards/7/sweep?force=true"
```

mina: sweep returned 202 Accepted. background compaction started: compaction-job-4512. estimating ~8-12m to reduce resident pages.

sarah.lee: meanwhile we should reduce incoming traffic to pool. can we shift 30% of traffic to 'inference-nvlink-reserve' standby pool? that pool is larger but slightly more expensive.

devon: yep, updating routing policy now. `PATCH /routing/pools/inference-gtx12` set weight=0.7, inference-nvlink-reserve weight=0.3.

deploy-bot: ROUTE_UPDATE: routing change deployed by @devon at 2966660103. policy-id rp-7783.

devon: also toggled `RT_KV_EVICT_AGGRESSIVENESS=0.75` on runtime config for pool. this will force earlier evictions. expect increased token latency for a bit.

oncall-sre: node-14 behavior: still OOMing after sweep started, repeated container restarts. I'd recommend cordon+recreate to force a fresh node.

ravi: will cordon now: `kubectl cordon node-14 && kubectl drain node-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`

ops-bot: K8S: node-14 cordoned by @ravi at 2966660189. Pods evicted, new pods scheduled to nodes 18-19.

mina: compaction job progress: 55% complete at 2966660200. resident bytes on shard-7 down ~18% since start. eviction counter rising. good sign.

devon: attention pager logs showing fewer page_in failures but still some CUDA OOM spikes on node-15. might be fragmentation in allocator. need a runtime restart with allocator flag enabling slab-defrag.

sarah.lee: schedule a rolling restart of runtime on nodes 12-17 with `--allocator-defrag=on` in env to allow background defrag pass. do one node at a time.

ravi: starting restart on node-15 now. will watch.

ops-bot: INFRA: rolling-restart job restart-runtime-2966660285 started by @ravi. nodes to touch: 15,12,13,16,17.

devon: logs from restart on node-15: allocator reports reclaimed pages and fragmentation metric dropped from 0.82 -> 0.34. no OOMs observed on restart target after bringup.

mina: compaction job done at 2966660345. shard-7 resident now stable, page-in error rate dropped to baseline.

sarah.lee: current customer impact: a subset of long-context requests experienced 503s for ~20-35m and elevated latency for ~40m. downstream: 3 customers reported degraded responses, CS ticketed.

oncall-sre: mitigation summary: sweep + aggressive eviction + routing shift + node cordon + allocator-defrag restart. recommend follow-ups: 1) schedule automatic hourly compaction for high-churn shards; 2) add compaction-runbook to runbook repo; 3) tweak default evict aggressiveness for pool under high memory growth.

devon: creating INC-2026-042 follow-up ticket with postmortem checklist and owners. assigning to @sarah.lee for customer comms and @ravi for infra patch.

ops-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: INC-2026-042 severity reduced to SEV-2 at 2966660400.

sarah.lee: handing off to night oncall (@night-sre). summary: slow KV leak -> allocator fragmentation -> OOMs on inference-gtx12. major mitigations applied, monitoring looks green. full postmortem tomorrow. signing off for now. :thumbsup:

oncall-sre: acknowledged handoff. leaving slack pinned links: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-042 , runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-compaction
